pages.text: The Akaishi Miner is a fixed 9x9x5 hollow multiblock: only the bottom and top decks are full cross-shaped plates (24 upgrade spots U each, 48 in total); the middle three layers remain open and are connected only by four pillars and the center column.$(br2)The preview is centered on the Drill Bit (0) at the bottom; above it are Framework → Controller (C) → Framework → Port (P).$(br2)Pillar example: the north and west pillars and the pillar bodies use regular Framework (X/F); the south pillar (S) is topped with one Miner Framework (External); the east pillar (E) carries a single Energy Input near the top. Framework (External), Energy Input and Item Output are interchangeable external blocks, limited to at most one per pillar (north and west show none); remaining pillar slots are filled with regular Framework. This is an example only; any combination of the four pillar blocks forms the structure.

$(bold)Build order:$(reset)$(li)Pillars: from the planned center, count 4 blocks in each cardinal direction and raise a 5-block pillar. Each level may be Miner Framework, Framework (External), Energy Input or Item Output; the last three are interchangeable external blocks sharing one spot per pillar, limited to at most one in total per pillar at any height; fill the rest of the pillar with Miner Framework$(li)Center column: stack Drill Bit → Framework → Controller → Framework → Port at the exact center (the 0 in the diagram marks the Drill Bit, the origin indicator)$(li)Two decks: fill the bottom and top cross plates with Framework and Upgrade Frames (24 spots each); keep the middle three layers hollow$(br2)$(bold)Formed state:$(reset) the controller checks continuously; removing or misplacing any required block (for example two external blocks on one pillar) collapses the miner.$(br2)$(bold)Open space:$(reset) every spot outside the required blocks (the hollow zone, corners and gaps between cross arms) may be filled freely without breaking the machine. Once formed, the Drill Bit projects a beacon beam straight down, making a working miner visible at distance.

$(bold)Drill Bit$(reset): located at the bottom of the center column, on the same axis as the controller. It is the preview anchor point and emits a beacon beam straight down while the structure is formed. It is a required block; breaking it collapses the miner. To stop mining without dismantling the structure, break the Drill Bit or the controller.

$(bold)Miner Energy Input$(reset): a power input for the pillar blocks. It has its own 10M energy buffer for pipes and, once formed, forwards power to the controller without a rate cap. Its interface shows the local charge and formed state; before forming it only stores energy and never sends. It accepts power only.

$(bold)Miner Item Output$(reset): an item output for the pillar blocks. It has a 27-slot product buffer that the controller fills with mined ores. It has priority over the Miner Port: once installed it is filled first, the port receives only the overflow, and items already in the port are transferred to it. The buffer is read-only; hoppers and item pipes can only extract. Together with the Energy Input and Framework (External) it counts as an external block: each pillar accepts at most one of the three in total, so they must be placed on different pillars.

$(bold)Miner Framework (External)$(reset): a structural block that differs in appearance from the regular Framework and is valid only on pillar spots; cross beams and the center column do not accept it. It has no interfaces but counts as an external block together with Energy Inputs and Item Outputs: at most one per pillar. Remaining pillar slots are filled with regular Framework.
Once the frame is built, proceed in order: select a controller to set the tier, add upgrade modules, then connect power from the Port and Energy Inputs to the grid.
